turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Well, I'm here because... I've gotten to the point where I plan my whole summer around avoiding wasps. It's just getting out of hand. 

I actually gave up my volunteer garden jobs at the church because of it. And at home, if I even hear a buzzing sound, I make my husband unload things by the back porch. I just refuse to go out there. It's really dictating what I can and can't do every day, so I thought I should finally come in and talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient describes extensive active avoidance of wasps that dictates daily life, including giving up church volunteer gardening and refusing to go out to the back porch.

turns.doctor_question: Besides wasps, are there other insects or situations that trigger similar intense fear or avoidance in you?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just the wasps. I mean, I don't love spiders or anything, but they don't make me panic like this. It's just the wasps, really.
